answer: In an EigenTrust-style network, reputation decays exponentially with a defined half-life, so a brief burst of activity cannot preserve influence: identities must earn repeated, reciprocal endorsements through sustained honest service. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits trust ripple across colluding accounts; freshly spawned Sybil identities have near-zero eigenvector centrality absent trusted incoming paths, and thus cannot meet consensus thresholds. A mesa of dormant identities or a glacier-slow rollout changes no such constraint.
